entities.summary: Vladimir Vladimirovich Nabokov, also known by the pen name Vladimir Sirin, was a Russian and American novelist, poet, translator, and entomologist. Born in Imperial Russia in 1899, Nabokov wrote his first nine novels in Russian (1926–1938) while living in Berlin, where he met his wife, Véra Nabokov. He achieved international acclaim and prominence after moving to the United States, where he began writing in English. Trilingual in Russian, English, and French, Nabokov became a U.S. citizen in 1945 and lived mostly on the East Coast before returning to Europe in 1961, where he settled in Montreux, Switzerland.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a renowned novelist and poet, Nabokov's works have had a significant impact on modern literature, with his novels such as 'Lolita' and 'Pale Fire' influencing generations of writers. His unique blend of style and thematic depth has cemented his place in literary history.
